title: Layman's Handbook: A Journey to SELF
author: Dr. Kadrin Artur
target_audience: Adults seeking personal growth and self-awareness
Individuals interested in self-discovery and spiritual exploration
People facing life transitions or searching for purpose
primary_purpose: To provide accessible, practical guidance for individuals embarking on a journey of self-discovery and personal transformation, using simple language and relatable analogies to make spiritual and psychological concepts understandable to everyone.

structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic chapters reflecting stages of self-discovery, each including explanations, reflection points, and practical exercises
features: Simple graphics or illustrations (in print version)

key_concepts_lessons: Understanding the nature of the 'self' and how it differs from ego or social identity
Recognizing the impact of conditioning and how to break free from limiting mental patterns
Viewing personal challenges as opportunities for growth, not limitations
Integrating spiritual insights into everyday living
Self-acceptance as the foundation for sustained happiness and transformation
notable_features: Written specifically for laypeople without jargon
Emphasis on actionable steps and exercises
Synthesizes Western psychology and Eastern philosophy
cultural_historical_context: Published post-pandemic, the book aims to address a growing global need for personal meaning and self-inquiry, using inclusive language and universal analogies to demystify self-help concepts.
reception_impact: Appreciated for its approachable and gentle guidance
Praised by readers new to spirituality for its clarity and practical advice
Used in workshops and group discussions on self-awareness
Some advanced readers may find it basic, but it is often recommended as a starting point
comparable_titles: The Untethered Soul by Michael A. Singer
Who Will Cry When You Die? by Robin Sharma
The Art of Happiness by Dalai Lama and Howard Cutler
You Can Heal Your Life by Louise Hay
